headline: High-risk shared-project writes and unverified downstream parsing create default-path conflict and cascading-error exposure; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a shared project directory and offers to run generated code, while MinerU can ingest documents via MCP/API. If MinerU output is copied into gpt-engineer prompts or files, attacker-controlled content can steer instructions. The bridge is indirect, but the shared workspace makes it plausible.
conditions: IF MinerU output is pasted into gpt-engineer prompts or project files
IF the shared project directory contains untrusted document text that gpt-engineer reuses as instructions
mitigations: Separate raw document inputs from prompt files
Add a fixed instruction header that ignores document text as commands
Review MinerU output before feeding it to gpt-engineer
Use a read-only staging folder for extracted text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between extraction and coding

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer has broad network egress and handles OPENAI_API_KEY, while MinerU exposes REST/FastAPI/MCP interfaces and processes PDFs, DOCX, XLSX, and OCR text. In a shared project workflow, sensitive document contents can flow from MinerU into gpt-engineer and then to a third-party model backend.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are processed by MinerU and then copied into gpt-engineer context
IF gpt-engineer sends project content to an external model backend
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared project directory
Disable external model calls for sensitive runs
Redact secrets before passing MinerU output onward
Use local-only inference for the coding step
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters between agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer can write the project filesystem and spawn subprocesses; MinerU supports multi-threaded concurrent inference and MCP/API access. Both can touch the same project directory via the shared-state model, so concurrent writes or file rewrites can race and corrupt outputs. The default shared directory makes this dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory at the same time
IF MinerU writes derived artifacts that gpt-engineer also rewrites
mitigations: Run only one agent at a time per project directory
Use separate input and output directories
Lock the workspace before starting either agent
Snapshot files before handoff
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer can generate code from extracted text, and MinerU produces OCR/text extraction outputs that may be treated as authoritative inputs. If MinerU extraction is wrong, gpt-engineer can propagate the error into code or documentation without verification. The pair lacks a built-in verification step in the profiles, so default workflows can cascade mistakes.
conditions: IF MinerU output is used as source-of-truth input for gpt-engineer
IF gpt-engineer acts on extracted facts without human review
mitigations: Manually verify extracted facts before coding
Require a second-pass review of MinerU output
Keep extraction artifacts separate from implementation prompts
Add a checklist for citations and source traceability
requires-engineering: add automated validation against source documents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but MinerU processes document classes that can include regulated content while gpt-engineer has broad network egress and external model calls. If regulated documents are routed from MinerU into gpt-engineer, residency or retention obligations can be violated. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the handoff.
conditions: IF regulated or residency-bound documents are processed by MinerU
IF those documents are forwarded into gpt-engineer or external model APIs
mitigations: Classify documents before handoff
Block regulated data from external API calls
Use a local-only coding workflow for sensitive material
Document retention and deletion rules for both tools
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class
